record.original_question: Let (W,S) be a finite Coxeter system and let u <= v in W. Writing the R-polynomial in the form ~R_{u,v}(t) = Q_{u,v}(t^2) when ell(u,v) is even and ~R_{u,v}(t) = t Q_{u,v}(t^2) when ell(u,v) is odd, must the polynomial Q_{u,v}(t) always be log-concave?

evidence.quote: More precisely, there is a polynomial Q_{u,v}(t) in N[t] such that ~R_{u,v}(t) = Q_{u,v}(t^2) if ell(u,v) is even and ~R_{u,v}(t) = t Q_{u,v}(t^2) if ell(u,v) is odd.
Conjecture 2.4. Let (W,S) be a finite Coxeter system and u,v in W, u <= v. Then the polynomial Q_{u,v}(t) is log-concave.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite Coxeter system, with length function $\ell:W\to\mathbb{N}$ and Bruhat order $\le$. For $u,v\in W$ with $u\le v$, write $\ell(u,v):=\ell(v)-\ell(u)$. Recall the (normalized) Kazhdan–Lusztig $R$-polynomials $\widetilde R_{u,v}(t)\in\mathbb{N}[t]$ characterized by $\widetilde R_{u,u}(t)=1$ and the recurrence
\[
\widetilde R_{u,v}(t)=\widetilde R_{su,sv}(t)+t\,\widetilde R_{su,v}(t)\quad\text{if }s\in S\text{ with }\ell(sv)<\ell(v),\ \ell(su)<\ell(u),
\]
\[
\widetilde R_{u,v}(t)=\widetilde R_{su,sv}(t)\quad\text{if }s\in S\text{ with }\ell(sv)<\ell(v),\ \ell(su)>\ell(u).
\]
It is known that $\widetilde R_{u,v}(t)$ is a polynomial in $\mathbb{N}[t]$ whose nonzero terms all have the same parity as $\ell(u,v)$. Hence there exists a unique polynomial $Q_{u,v}(t)\in\mathbb{N}[t]$ such that
\[
\widetilde R_{u,v}(t)=\begin{cases}Q_{u,v}(t^2) & \text{if } \ell(u,v)\text{ is even},\\ t\,Q_{u,v}(t^2) & \text{if } \ell(u,v)\text{ is odd}.\end{cases}
\]
A polynomial $\sum_{i\ge 0} a_i t^i\in\mathbb{R}[t]$ is called log-concave if $a_i^2\ge a_{i-1}a_{i+1}$ for all $i\ge 1$.

Question: Is it true that for every finite Coxeter system $(W,S)$ and every pair $u,v\in W$ with $u\le v$, the polynomial $Q_{u,v}(t)$ is log-concave?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture appears in a recent compilation of open problems on Coxeter groups and unimodality by Brenti (2024). No proof or counterexample for log-concavity of $Q_{u,v}(t)$ in arbitrary finite Coxeter systems was found in the literature search; the problem appears to be currently open, supported only by computational evidence and partial results.

status_evidence.title: Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials: History, Problems, and Combinatorial Invariance (Brenti)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of conjectures concerning unimodality and log-concavity for KL and R-polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: Log-concavity-type conjectures for KL/R-polynomials are listed among open problems.

status_evidence.title: Kazhdan–Lusztig R-polynomials, combinatorial invariance, and hypercube decompositions
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on R-polynomial structure; no proof of log-concavity of Q_{u,v} given.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the log-concavity conjecture is provided.
